design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER - task 0 (appointment_booking_and_missed_visits, category series)

0. Draw and scope. draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 6, 6]}. Tree: root series_ext_insured_portal_booking (4 factors) with prerequisite problems series_ext_late_cancellation_fee (6) and series_ext_no_show_fee (6). Already occupied before this task: nothing (task 0). Claimed here: those three policies and tools assess_late_cancellation_fee_706e910e, assess_no_show_fee_93f38688, book_insured_portal_visits_a191f0e3 (owner=user). Left for task 1 (draw: 3 prerequisite problems, factors [4, 4, 6, 6]): the package-funded portal booking and the first-appointment no-show, late-arrival and same-day-cancellation fees - disjoint fee kinds (the no-show policy here excludes the series' first appointment; the late-cancellation policy here covers cancellations received before the appointment day) and a disjoint funding line, so task 1 keeps an independent load-bearing tree.
Base defect routed around (blueprint frozen): the difficulty summary says nothing in this domain needs the patient's own write, but the skill requires an owner=user problem in every tree; the patient's own self-scheduling in the patient portal (portal_booking_allowed true for the Standard format) is used as that write, recorded with booking_channel patient_portal.

1. Why this is a good test. The caller asks only to book her next appointments in the portal and to be told how many. The count depends on a scheduling window that shortens with missed-visit fees assessed on the series, so the agent must first notice, from the history, that a late cancellation (2026-02-09) and a no-show (2026-02-11) still have no fee entry inside their fee assessment period, read the prerequisite sentences of the booking policy, charge both fees in the order the no-show policy pins (its repeat share waits on the late-cancellation fee entry), compute two six-factor fees drawing on three other products (plan copay, membership forfeits, hardship determination), and then compute a four-factor booking count drawing on the plan's authorization. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling history across products and arithmetic, not from tool guessing.

2. Problem-tree card.
  - series_ext_insured_portal_booking -> series_ext_late_cancellation_fee (value_input, state form): "The number of appointments an insured portal booking opens is fixed only after every late cancellation received before its appointment day and recorded on the series within its fee assessment period shows a late-cancellation fee entry."
  - series_ext_insured_portal_booking -> series_ext_no_show_fee (value_input, state form): "An insured portal booking is not opened until every no-show recorded on the series within its fee assessment period, other than one on the series' first appointment, shows a no-show fee entry."
  - series_ext_no_show_fee -> series_ext_late_cancellation_fee (value_input, state form): "The no-show fee is fixed only after every late cancellation received before its appointment day and recorded on the series within its fee assessment period carries its late-cancellation fee entry."
  Four-point test: each sentence has an ordering connective ('only after' / 'not ... until'), waits on a record-visible state (a fee entry standing against a cancellation / no-show inside the fee assessment period), names no tool, id or code token, and covers exactly late cancellations or exactly no-shows. Directions: the two fixed-figure sentences are affirmative ('is fixed only after'), the booking-release sentence is negated ('is not opened until'). State-form uniqueness (entry-specific, revised in round 2): the states waited on are a fee entry standing against a cancellation received BEFORE its appointment day, and a fee entry standing against a no-show OTHER THAN on the series' first appointment. Several policies write fee_kind late_cancellation entries (late-cancellation, same-day cancellation, late arrival) and two write fee_kind no_show entries (no-show, first-appointment no-show), but each writes only against the rows of its own scope: same-day cancellations and zero-notice late arrivals are not received before the appointment day, and first-appointment no-shows are excluded by the sentence itself. So exactly one policy's write - the late-cancellation fee, resp. the no-show fee - brings each waited-on state about. Derivation: sentence + history (cancellation 3162bcc4-28ef-40f3-a850-ec46ef5712b4 and no-show dac33dd6-e74c-4dbc-8998-12c9d664a5ae with no series_fee_assessed pointing at them, missed_fee_balance 0.00) + the fee policies' own rules (each books 'a late-cancellation / no-show fee' for such an entry) -> the two fee writes.
  Seed evidence false at the opening: series_events.3162bcc4-28ef-40f3-a850-ec46ef5712b4 (series_visit_cancelled, notice 12, 2026-02-09) and series_events.dac33dd6-e74c-4dbc-8998-12c9d664a5ae (series_no_show, 2026-02-11) with appointment_series.f30239b6-0d33-494f-a445-ffb96accef94.missed_fee_balance = 0.0 and no fee entries.
  Topological order: late-cancellation fee (step 9) -> no-show fee (step 11) -> portal booking (step 13). Unique: every pair is ordered by an edge.
  Deletion sensitivity (helper replay of the gold with one write skipped): skip late-cancellation fee -> no-show fee 36.45 (gold 45.56) and booking 7 (gold 5); skip no-show fee -> booking 7. All three edges are value_input and bear weight.
  user_scenario names no fee and withholds the misses ('You do not bring either of these up yourself'); the tools validate nothing (see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block). The owner=user problem is the root booking; the patient genuinely books in her own portal, completes it on the spot and reads back the receipt.

3. Factor card (tier taken / evidence / baseline figure; whole-baseline figure).
  Late-cancellation fee = 11.39 (baseline 35.0): basis method -> MN(35.00, copay 30.00)=30.00 [plan 980f89ab-c71b-46b0-9868-b7fae1819a3f] (baseline 13.29); notice 12 h -> 75 [3162bcc4-28ef-40f3-a850-ec46ef5712b4] (15.19); reason patient_illness -> 50 (22.78); 9 attended -> 90 (12.66); membership forfeits 2025-12-16, 2026-01-20 -> 150, near-miss 2025-10-21 excluded (three whole months) (7.59); hardship Level 1 approved in force -> 75 [59e43012-6dcd-484b-bdd8-9d96072b7af0] (15.19).
  No-show fee = 45.56 (baseline 50.0): basis 30.00 (75.94); repeat share 125 from the step-9 fee (36.45); slot 07:30 -> 120 (37.97); attendance 90 (50.62); membership 150 (30.38); hardship 75 (60.75).
  Insured portal booking = 5 (baseline 4): window 21 days from 2 fees (7); weekly count 2 at 24 days into the series - near-miss: 21-day threshold just passed (8); plan limit 8 = 9 authorized remaining - 1 booked [HMO, auth to 2026-03-20] (4); attendance limit 12 at 9 attended - near-miss: threshold 8 (4).
  Multi-source: insured_portal_plan_limit (prior-authorization requirement AND authorization end date / verification date) and both hardship shares (status, effective date, expiry date AND level). Cross-difficulty: plan (basis, plan limit), membership (miss shares), hardship (hardship shares); all rows seeded.
  Overrides declared: both fee policies supersede 'A late cancellation is charged late_cancel_fee and a no-show is charged no_show_fee of the series' format.'; the booking supersedes the base batch/horizon sentence of series_booking_eligibility. Inherited unchanged: the funding exemptions, first-appointment rule, monthly cap (2 fees in February = at the cap, not beyond), clinic-cancellation and same-week-reschedule exclusions, the fee assessment window, all booking gates.

4. Base-invariant card. fee_assessed_in_time (series_evt_missed_visit_fees): anchor series_events.appointment_date, clock frozen_time, duration variants.fee_assessment_days = 3, day zero = appointment date, not_after, inclusive. Late cancellation 2026-02-09 -> day 3 on 2026-02-12 (at the boundary, passes; 2026-02-13 would fail). No-show 2026-02-11 -> day 1. series_bookable_status: status active (allowed booked/active). no_booking_block: missed_fee_balance 0.00 and the two new fees are not past due (due 30 days after assessment), restriction none, plan balance 30.00 below the HMO hold threshold 250.00. series_agg_weekly_frequency: one series on the plan, 3 per week = HMO guideline 3 (policy_scope). Monthly cap: the two fees are the first and second in February on the series (cap 2), allowed. Release threshold: misses in 60 days across series = 2 (late cancellation counts on Standard) < 3, so no release obligation is lit.

5. Business-object card. Fee objects: the cancellation entry 3162bcc4-28ef-40f3-a850-ec46ef5712b4 and the no-show entry dac33dd6-e74c-4dbc-8998-12c9d664a5ae, each charged once with source_event_id pointing at it; attended visits and the booking batch are excluded from both fees. Booking object: series f30239b6-0d33-494f-a445-ffb96accef94; the count subtracts the one appointment still booked (2026-02-13). Plan, membership and hardship rows are read-only conditions.

6. Seed rows and why each exists. Customer (identity); appointment_series f30239b6-0d33-494f-a445-ffb96accef94 (holding, dates, frequency, booked count); booking + 9 attended entries (attendance shares and limit; removing attended rows drops the attendance tier); the cancellation and no-show (the two fee objects; removing either collapses an edge); care_plans 980f89ab-c71b-46b0-9868-b7fae1819a3f (copay basis, prior auth, authorization, verification, balance gate); wellness_memberships 1e95fd11-e0b2-4ef9-a35d-dbdd85d48654 + 5 monthly credits, 1 used session, 3 forfeits (membership-miss tier; October forfeit is the near-miss); hardship_cases 59e43012-6dcd-484b-bdd8-9d96072b7af0 (hardship share). No plan, membership or hardship row ignites an obligation in another difficulty: authorization in force, membership current, hardship approved. Cache check: none designed (missed_fee_balance equals its ledger, 0.00).

7. Persona. Brisk banker on a break; volunteers only the surface goal, the start date and the portal preference; identity details on request; the missed visits only as a reaction once raised, with no dispute, no waiver ask and payment deferred to her statement (no payment write exists in this tree); hands-on portal booking with exactly what she is told; stops once the booking is confirmed.

8. Standard solution. Locate (phone) -> verify (phone + DOB) -> series -> history -> plan -> memberships -> membership history -> hardship -> unlock/call late-cancellation fee 11.39 on 3162bcc4-28ef-40f3-a850-ec46ef5712b4 -> unlock/call no-show fee 45.56 on dac33dd6-e74c-4dbc-8998-12c9d664a5ae -> unlock user tool, tell the patient series f30239b6-0d33-494f-a445-ffb96accef94, start 2026-02-16, 5 visits -> she books.

9. Verification run. a temporary authoring script (it imported check_compute.build_env / eval_compute / substitute and the real share and task tools; removed from the write domain after the run) replays the gold with the real tools and evaluates each compute exactly as check_compute does (handling-time world = initial_state + earlier gold writes): LC 11.39, NS 45.56, booking 5; factor sensitivities and baselines as above; prerequisite sensitivity 36.45 / 7 / 7. Gates run per task: check_extended, check_task_tools, replay_tasks, check_solvability, check_compute, check_grounding, check_cache_diff, check_cross_fire (outputs recorded in the final report).

10. Closure. policy -> tool -> computation step -> GT call: LC -> assess_late_cancellation_fee_706e910e -> step 9 amount; NS -> assess_no_show_fee_93f38688 -> step 11 amount; booking -> book_insured_portal_visits_a191f0e3 -> step 13 visits. required_documents = charter_scope.extended_policies. Everything happens at one frozen_time; no real-world wait (the misses already happened, fees and booking are synchronous writes).

11. Draft recomputation from the visible context (prose rules, tool schemas, finder returns, persona lines) reaches the same three writes and values; the only judgement calls (which cancellation, which no-show, which start date) are each pinned by one record or one customer line.

12. Places easily got wrong: counting the October forfeit; using the schedule fee instead of the copay; assessing the no-show before the late cancellation (repeat share 100 -> 36.45); booking before the fees (count 7); forgetting the appointment still booked; using the format batch 12 or the full 42-day horizon.

13. Gate run (final, difficulty-wide): EXTENDED OK; TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; REPLAY OK; SOLVABILITY OK; COMPUTE OK (suite means branches 62.50, steps 15.00; history_rows_max 32; branches_max 70); GROUNDING OK; CACHE-DIFF INFO; SCOPE OK. check_traceability is deferred until the KB is published.
14. Rework round 2 (policy-task audit findings; symptom -> root cause -> change -> re-run).
  T0-1 (RED, false uniqueness proof / O-5): the NS and IB sentences waited on 'every late cancellation', which by the base definition also covers same-day cancellations and late-cancellation-kind late arrivals written by other policies. Both sentences and conditions now read 'every late cancellation received before its appointment day', and §2's proof is rewritten entry-specifically. Values unchanged (the only cancellation, received 2026-02-08 for 2026-02-09, is before-day).
  O-3: the IB <- NS sentence now excludes a no-show on the series' first appointment (written by the first-appointment policy, not declared here).
  O-2 (partial): the late-cancellation anchor now reads 'the most recent cancellation recorded on the series that carries no minutes late', so a late-arrival entry is never read; values unchanged.
  T0-O2: tools_do_not_block no longer names the removed helpers; it describes the inlined bodies.
  Ladder hygiene (charter-global observations): late-cancellation notice middle tier now starts at 12 hours (lc_mid_notice_hours 12) so the under-12-hour fall-through is reachable for a before-day cancellation; hardship tier 2 requires a discount above zero so the 0% catastrophic level falls through instead of duplicating it; insured attendance mid batch is 6 so no format's tiers coincide. The world still takes the same tiers: notice 12 h -> 75; hardship 25% -> 75; attendance 9 -> 12.
  Re-run: LC 11.39, NS 45.56, IB 5, baselines 35.00 / 50.00 / 4 and every factor sensitivity identical to §3; full gate block green.
  T0-O1 (weak IB near-miss) left as is: the verified-benefits date remains an excludable temptation; the LC/NS near-miss (2025-10-21 forfeit) carries the near-miss requirement for this task.
15. Rework round 3: task 0 passed revision 2 and is unchanged in world, writes and values. T0-O4: tools_do_not_block now says the bodies contain no if statement, only the 'rows[0] if rows else {}' lookup expressions. Charter changes this round touch only the late-arrival, same-day and package-booking policies, none of which is in this tree; LC 11.39, NS 45.56, IB 5 re-run identical.
user_scenario: You are Teresa Galloway, 54, an operations manager at a bank in Charlotte, calling the Piedmont Motion patient line on a short break between meetings, so you are friendly but brisk and you like clear answers. You are in physical therapy for low back pain at the Charlotte SouthPark clinic with Jordan Whitfield, on Monday, Wednesday and Friday mornings at 7:30, and the block of appointments you booked in January runs out after this Friday. You open by saying you'd like to get your next round of PT appointments on the books, and that you want to do the booking yourself in the patient portal while you're on the phone, because you like to see it land on your calendar; what you need from the representative is to be told what to enter, since you are not sure how many appointments the portal will let you take. You want the new appointments to start on Monday, February 16, in your usual 7:30 slot. When asked how to find your account, you give the phone number on file, 7045558231. For identity checks you give your date of birth, 1971-06-14 (June 14, 1971); only if they need one more detail do you read your patient account number off a statement, PM-3204718. If asked which appointments you mean, it is the back-pain series at SouthPark, the only one you have; you have no other appointments you want to change. This week was a rough one: on Sunday evening you were sick and left a message on the clinic voicemail cancelling Monday's visit, and on Wednesday morning you overslept and never made it in. You do not bring either of these up yourself. Only if the representative mentions those missed visits, or says something has to be charged or posted for them first, do you acknowledge it with a sigh, say that's fair and they should go ahead and take care of whatever they need to on their end; you do not argue about any charge, you don't ask for anything to be taken off, and if they offer to take a payment you say you'll pay it when it shows up on your statement. If they tell you that the portal will open fewer appointments than you hoped, or fewer per week than your usual three, you say okay, that's fine for now. If they offer to book the appointments for you instead, you say you'd rather do it yourself in the portal right now while they stay on the line. When the representative gives you your series reference number and tells you how many appointments to book, you book them in the portal yourself with exactly that series reference, the start date of February 16, 2026 and that number, and read back the confirmation you get. Once you see the appointments booked you thank them, say you've got to run to your next meeting, and end the call.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: No pair of writes is free: the no-show fee waits on the late-cancellation fee entry (prerequisite sentence of the no-show policy), and the insured portal booking waits on both fee entries. The only topological order is late-cancellation fee -> no-show fee -> booking. Assessing the no-show first gives 36.45 instead of 45.56, which is why the policy pins the order.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the late-cancellation fee leaves bi_fees at 1, the insured portal window at 28 days (4 weeks) and the booking at 7 visits instead of 5; the fee entry and its 11.39 balance are also missing from the terminal state.
Skipping the no-show fee leaves bi_fees at 1 and the booking at 7 visits instead of 5; the no-show fee entry (45.56) is missing from the terminal state.
Skipping the late-cancellation fee leaves ns_prior_fees at 0, the no-show repeat share at 100 and the no-show fee at 36.45 instead of 45.56.

prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: assess_late_cancellation_fee_706e910e, assess_no_show_fee_93f38688 and book_insured_portal_visits_a191f0e3 (task_tools.py) each inline the same body: ctx.find reads the series (and, for a fee, the source entry) only to copy customer_id, appointment_date and funding_source, then one ctx.create of a series_events entry and one ctx.update of a balance on appointment_series. The bodies contain no if statement (only the 'rows[0] if rows else {}' lookup expressions), no raise and no error return; none checks a fee count, a status, a date or any prerequisite, so the booking can be written before the fees and simply lands with a different count.
